extracted.intended_audience: mathematics educators and education researchers (post-secondary instructors, assessment designers, and equity-focused scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: A glossary of terms and metrics used in mathematics education research and equitable instructional design, aimed at clarifying concepts used in assessment, classroom discourse, and equity analytics. Useful for educators designing inclusive instruction and researchers analyzing participation and learning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academically productive talk
rubrics_metrics.description: Classroom discourse that promotes student learning and understanding, and encourages students to engage in academic discussions. This higher-level academic discourse helps students recognize, build on, and respond to the thinking of the teacher and their peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a desired attribute of classroom interactions; implies facilitation practices that surface and connect student reasoning rather than closed-answer recitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Access means that everyone can exist in a space in their full humanity and have their varied needs respected and met. Ensuring access is both a matter of accessible design (i.e., flexible practices that generally work for a lot of different people), and specific accommodations for individual needs that are not adequately addressed by your overall design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat access as both universal design and individualized accommodation; aim to design practices that work broadly while providing specific supports when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The things that an individual needs to access a space. Access needs are many and can be varied, including: 1. Physical access and ergonomics 2. Opportunities to move, stretch, and take breaks 3. Food, drinks, appropriate bathrooms 4. Language/communication that is understandable 5. Safety, trust, and nonjudgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or designing learning environments, enumerate and accommodate these varied needs; use both environmental design and case-by-case accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active learning
rubrics_metrics.description: A phrase used primarily in higher education, which refers to classrooms in which students engage in a variety of activities (as compared to pure lecture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies instructional designs with interactive tasks, discussion, problem solving, or other student-centered activities; contrasted with direct/lecture-based instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigning competence is the practice of explicitly elevating the status of students perceived as low status by highlighting their meaningful contributions in public spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classroom practice to correct participation/status imbalances — e.g., publicly crediting contributions from marginalized students to change perceptions of competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric that accounts for the size of various demographic groups when looking at equity data. Calculated by dividing the overall number of contributions for each group by the number of students in the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a per-capita contribution measure to compare groups fairly. Example: 8 contributions from 4 Black students → average contributions = 2; 16 contributions from 20 Latinx students → average contributions = 0.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behaviorism
rubrics_metrics.description: A theory of learning that emphasizes the role of reinforcement and punishment in shaping behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A theoretical lens for designing and evaluating instructional interventions that use rewards, feedback schedules, and observable performance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bodymind
rubrics_metrics.description: A term that acknowledges that human experience is embodied, recognizing that bodies and minds exist together, and our bodies influence the way that we experience the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a conceptual stance when evaluating accessibility, pedagogy, and student experience — emphasizes embodied factors in learning and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen’s d
rubrics_metrics.description: A statistical measure of the difference between two groups (i.e., effect size), calculated by dividing the difference between the means of the groups by the standard deviation of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an effect-size metric when reporting and comparing intervention outcomes; interpret magnitude with commonly used benchmarks and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex Instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex Instruction is a set of instructional practices grounded in sociological theory that focuses on the concept of status. High status students tend to have more opportunities to participate, and their ideas are seen as more valuable. Consequently, targeting status as a site of intervention can be a useful strategy for remedying racial (and other) inequities in math classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employs four primary strategies to reduce status imbalances and promote student belonging (status interventions). Use as a framework for designing equitable group work and participation structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructivism
rubrics_metrics.description: A theory of learning that emphasizes the active construction of knowledge by learners, through their experiences and interactions with the world. A key tenet is that students are not blank slates, but that all new knowledge must be built on prior knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate or design curricula and tasks that connect new ideas to students’ prior understanding and support active sense-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: A teacher-centered approach to instruction that emphasizes teacher-led lectures, drills, and practice activities (i.e., lecture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts with active learning; evaluate appropriateness based on learning goals, student needs, and context. Often discussed when weighing trade-offs between efficiency and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction (of feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: The direction of feedback focuses on whether it aims to highlight something positive (strengths) or negative (areas of growth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing or assessing feedback, consider balance and alignment with goals: formative growth-oriented feedback vs. evaluative/critical feedback; choose direction to support learning and equity.
